# MRVL model conventions and limits

Version 2. Information cutoff: October 18, 2026. Research only. Dollars and share counts are millions unless marked otherwise.

## What the output means

The financial origin is August 1, 2026, the last reported balance sheet. A half-year convention discounts the remaining FY2027 cash flow for 0.5 years, followed by fifteen full fiscal years through FY2042. Information learned through October 18 informs those scenarios. This is a **retrospective-information operating DCF at an August financial origin**, not an August backtest and not an October equity value. There is no stock-price input, price target, recommended trade, scenario probability or upside percentage.

Actual FY2027 H1 revenue of 5,157.1 is removed from each full-year FY2027 revenue assumption. The stub therefore contains only H2 revenue. H1 data-center 4,004.2 and other 1,152.9 are removed from their respective categories. The forecast keeps these two disclosed end markets separate; it does not invent reported product-level profits. Company submarket aspirations inform the chosen totals but are never added on top of total data-center revenue. Annualized exit run-rates are not booked as full-year revenue.

The exact August 18 share inventory cannot be combined mechanically with this origin. New grants or exercises between August 1 and August 18 would require reconciling the post-origin grant-cost budget and the opening legal award pool. Actual October cash, share changes, vesting and warrant milestones also remain unknown. These are hard gates: the model outputs null for company per-share and current-date values.

## Revenue and profitability

All scenario paths, beyond disclosed actuals, are analyst judgments. Management's October targets are separately retained in operating-evidence-v2.json. The base case reaches FY2028 revenue of 18,000 versus management's 20,000, and FY2031 revenue of 45,000 versus 70,000–90,000. The management-delivery interpretation reaches 20,000 and 75,000 respectively, but its mix, expenses and cash conversion are still independent assumptions. Downside includes a 10% FY2029 sales contraction and slow recovery.

Revenue is modeled as cash-equivalent customer consideration before amortization of existing equity warrants and after ordinary rebates. Whether every management target uses precisely this convention is unresolved. That limits direct percentage comparisons. Known customer warrants, including the August Google instrument, are reserved for the equity-claim layer. Their noncash accounting amortization must not also reduce this operating forecast. A separate 1% recurring future commercial-incentive charge, 1.5% downside, represents additional future customer concessions/awards, excluding the already inventoried warrants. It is an analyst allowance, not reported guidance.

Gross-margin and cash operating-cost budgets start before employee equity compensation and acquired-intangible accounting amortization. Ordinary equipment depreciation, technology amortization and operating rent remain embedded in costs. The model then subtracts a future grant-value charge once. It is not a GAAP forecast or a reconstruction of management's non-GAAP EPS. H2 base gross margin is 58%, consistent with the midpoint of Q3 guidance; upside uses 58.5%. Custom-silicon mix, supplier costs and customer bargaining limit long-term gross margin. R&D and commercial costs do not disappear in the terminal period.

Base terminal economic operating margin, with R&D expensed, is 28.5%: 55% gross margin minus 16% cash R&D, 3.5% cash SG&A, 6% future grants and 1% future commercial incentives. Downside is 23.5%; management-delivery is 30.5%. These differ intentionally from management's 44%–46% FY2031 non-GAAP operating target.

## Employee compensation without duplicate legacy costs

The annual-report grant tables imply gross value proxies of approximately 765.4, 686.6 and 810.7 for FY2024–FY2026, or 13.9%, 11.9% and 9.9% of revenue. These are rounded target-level grant-value estimates including an approximate ESPP component, not precise compensation expense or cash payment. PRSUs can settle differently from target. Acquisition retention creates further variability.

The base recurring future grant-value budget starts at 10% of revenue and fades to 6% by FY2037. Even with a declining percentage, the absolute budget expands materially with revenue. This is a cash-equivalent opportunity-cost method: as though future employee services were paid in cash rather than new stock. It permits a fixed opening-equity-claim allocation without also counting the same future grants as incremental shares. It does not assume future SBC is free.

Opening unvested awards/options are distinct claims on equity. Their remaining legacy GAAP amortization is not charged again on top of the future-grant budget. Gross existing-award claims also capture the value split between employee net shares and cash tax withholding on settlement; deducting that same withholding again from the equity-value calculation while retaining gross dilution would double count. This valuation rule does not eliminate the treasury cash payment. The separate monthly cash screen schedules legacy withholding under both future compensation policies, without changing economic FCFF or adding a second valuation deduction. Exact classification, strikes and performance probabilities must be resolved before actual share allocation. Neither ungranted plan reserves nor January awards are added to the later combined outstanding pool.

SBC sensitivities hold revenue, cash R&D, cash SG&A and gross margin fixed. The 70% R&D share of future grants is a rounded judgment anchored by FY2026 R&D SBC of 409.0 out of total 590.8. It changes only the research-capital diagnostic, not the underlying cash-equivalent FCFF identity. A separate flat 10%-forever grant-cost case tests the optimistic fading percentage.

## Research capitalization and tax

Five-year straight-line research life is an analyst assumption, not measured patent life. Historical R&D uses a single latest-reported comparative vintage. Spending is capitalized at year end, with no same-year amortization. The January research asset is rolled to August by adding actual H1 R&D and removing half a year's amortization of the five prior fiscal cohorts. The resulting opening research asset is a diagnostic 6,252.17.

Projected economic R&D equals cash R&D plus 70% of new-grant cost. Let NRI = economic R&D minus five-year research amortization. Economic EBIT = expensed-R&D EBIT + NRI. Cash taxes continue to apply to the expensed-R&D operating earnings, so economic NOPAT = expensed-R&D NOPAT + NRI. Total reinvestment includes NRI. Consequently:

FCFF = expensed-R&D NOPAT − nonresearch reinvestment
     = capitalized-R&D NOPAT − nonresearch reinvestment − NRI.

Research capitalization cannot manufacture value through an unmatched addback. Both forms are tested for every period. Research assets may decline when old spending exceeds new spending; the cash identity still holds.

Normalized operating cash tax begins at 15% base/upside and 18% downside, fading to 21%/23%. These are analyst cash-tax approximations, deliberately above the company's current 11% non-GAAP rate and the call's preliminary 13% FY2028 rate. The grant-cost deduction smooths eventual ordinary compensation tax benefits rather than asserting immediate legal grant-date deductibility. No extra stock-exercise tax windfall or deferred-tax-asset face value is added. Opening tax payables are separately deducted in the provisional claims bridge and excluded from forecast FCFF, preventing duplicate valuation subtraction. The treasury screen reserves their full cash amount at its opening; it does not treat a valuation deduction as spendable cash. Tax jurisdiction, grant timing and loss-carryforward realization remain sensitivity risks.

## Growth receives an explicit capital allowance

Opening identified operating NWC is 2,808.0, including long-term ship/debit and supply-capacity prepayments. It excludes cash, the forward derivative, tax/license/restructuring claims and unknown other balances. It is not claimed to be complete GAAP working capital. Unknown other assets and liabilities are excluded symmetrically, with capital-efficiency sensitivity rather than an invented net amount.

Capacity prepayments start at 487.0. H2 net capacity investment of 600 is an explicit analyst assumption; subsequent deposits grow toward 5% of annual revenue, without releases. It is not inferred by subtracting a net balance change from management's approximately 1,000 FY2027 gross payment expectation. Gross payments, consumption and reclassifications are not sufficiently disclosed for that reconciliation. The original 200–1,000 sensitivity is now labeled allocation/floor: a higher deposit can displace residual other investment. In base, 600 to 1,000 deposits raises aggregate H2 investment only 85.4375 and displaces 314.5625 of other investment. A separate additional-400 stress preserves H2 other investment and increases H2 total investment by the full 400. It reduces base EV by 378.9141, versus 80.9337 for the allocation/floor change. Later deposit balances can affect later capital floors, so even the new stress is not labeled an all-horizon fixed-capex experiment.

Other operating NWC grows toward 25% of annual revenue, or 30% downside. Combined with capacity deposits, the mature NWC target is 30%/35%. Opening minimum operating cash of 1,000, a judgment rather than management minimum, grows toward 8% of annual revenue; all increases reduce FCFF. No NWC/cash release is assumed on contraction. A contraction adds a 3%-of-sales lockup.

The aggregate nonresearch growth-funding allowance initially equals positive change in annual revenue scale divided by scenario sales-to-capital. It is floored at the explicit NWC and cash investment, ensuring those capital requirements are charged in operating FCFF. This arithmetic does not establish cash-financing availability. Remaining net investment goes to equipment, technology licenses and other operating assets. Adding ordinary D&A at 3.7% of sales produces a gross-investment allowance. This is a transparent aggregate capital budget, **not** an independently sourced physical-capex projection. Maintenance replacement is funded through D&A embedded in EBIT and its equal replacement allowance; growth capital comes on top. No new acquisitions are assumed. The acquired capabilities must grow through this operating/research spending; future purchases would require additional deductions.

The operating model excludes future settlement of opening debt-like license, restructuring and tax claims because the bridge deducts their opening amounts. Future ordinary technology purchases remain in operating investment. Operating leases remain expensed; their 323.2 liability is not also deducted. The 666.3 technology commitment total overlaps recognized licenses and is not an additional debt deduction. Ordinary foundry purchase commitments belong in future cost/capital budgets, with failure/cancellation risk in downside.

## Returns, horizon and terminal economics

Initial WACC is 11.43929%, from the separately dated rate/ERP/industry-beta inputs. A 5% target debt weight and 130-bp credit spread are judgments. It fades to 9% by FY2037. Stable growth is 2.5% downside, 3% base, 3.5% management-delivery, all below terminal WACC. FY2037–FY2042 gives the five-year research vintages time to reach a genuinely stable regime before terminal value.

Terminal reinvestment = next-period economic NOPAT × growth / incremental economic ROIC. The default **incremental** return is 9%, equal to terminal WACC. Competitive customer power, talent costs and technology substitution argue against assuming indefinite excess returns on new capital. This is not a measurement of actual MRVL ROIC, nor a claim that historical book capital immediately earns 9%. Existing accumulated-capital diagnostics use historical acquisition book amounts and should not be mistaken for replacement-cost returns. No market-calibrated ROIC is used.

The implied terminal nonresearch investment subtracts research net investment from total required investment. The sales-to-capital path fades to the implied value, rather than retaining a high-turnover growth assumption while imposing a lower terminal return. Terminal FCFF and research investment grow exactly at the selected stable growth rate from FY2042. A 12% incremental terminal-return sensitivity is separately labeled as requiring persistent new-capital advantage. Original WACC sensitivities are labeled coupled changes because default terminal ROIC moves with WACC. New pure-rate sensitivities fix terminal ROIC at 9%, leaving all operating FCFF and terminal FCFF unchanged. Base pure +1 percentage point WACC produces EV 83,731.523; pure −1 point produces 123,880.096. These are distinct from the coupled 86,728.711 and 117,859.866.

## Claims, liquidity and hard gates

The provisional August1 reported-fair-value bridge adds only 2,932.8 surplus cash and the separate 131.0 forward asset; subtracts 4,999.9 face debt, 749.5 earnout FV, 220.0 licenses, 238.4 restructuring and 249.4 opening tax payables. Net adjustment is −3,393.4 before employee and customer equity-option claims. Marketable/nonmarketable investments are excluded rather than treated as cash. The bridge is a disclosed election, not a finished company equity estimate.

A success-linked earnout treatment must replace the stale reported FV before producing scenario-specific equity values. Never deduct FV and also add earnout shares/cash. NVIDIA preferred participates as 21.778 common-equivalent shares; the 2,000 cash proceeds are already in August cash, with no second preferred-debt deduction. Google and older warrants require option value, vesting and exercise treatment. Full gross Google shares require matching exercise value; potential proceeds are not present cash. Out-of-the-money options can have time value. A synthetic-only simultaneous option allocator is tested; missing company inputs are not fabricated. It is not an approved MRVL contingent-claim model. Google revenue milestones, Celestial earnout achievement and common value are correlated; multiplying a vanilla call by an unsupported independent vesting probability is not sufficient. Resolve joint operating/claim states before any company equity allocation. Google qualifying revenue is measured August 1, 2026 through January 29, 2033; the distinct warrant expiry is August 18, 2033, subject to extensions.

## Treasury settlement and funding status

The v1 annual cash screen is superseded by **conditional monthly settlement sensitivities**, not by a complete actual treasury forecast. Seven cash-policy/timing cases are run for each operating scenario over 186 calendar months. Actual liquidity adequacy and forecast covenant compliance remain null. Funding results do not change enterprise EV or become a second equity bridge.

Reported H1 cash reconciles exactly: 2,638.8 opening + 1,244.3 CFO − 1,551.7 investing + 1,601.4 financing = 3,932.8 closing. Financing includes 365.2 employee withholding, 57.5 employee-plan proceeds, 107.7 dividends, 56.6 license payments and 400 repurchases. The 533.8 SBC CFO addback is noncash. H1 CFO less PP&E is 961.9; subtracting both categories of license cash gives 900.3; then withholding less employee proceeds gives 592.6; after dividends and repurchases, 84.9 remains. These are cash subtotals, not economic owner earnings. The primary statement and full line reconciliation are linked in historical-cash-reconciliation-v2.json.

Opening treasury surplus is 1,992 after reserving 1,000 operating cash plus 220 licenses, 238.4 restructuring, 249.4 taxes and maximum 233 earnout cash. All reserves stay unavailable. The cash earnout reserve is not stacked onto the separate 749.5 reported-FV valuation deduction.

Two alternative future-pay policies are explicit:

- **Literal cash replacement:** keep the new-grant economic cost as cash compensation, and also pay legacy withholding. This is a counterfactual employment-payment policy, not reported company practice.
- **Equity settlement:** add back the new-grant economic cost, reverse its modeled tax deduction, and deduct assumed future-cohort withholding. The illustrative cohorts vest one-quarter at 12, 24, 36 and 48 months; withholding is 35% of unchanged grant-value proxy. No unverified employee contributions, exercise proceeds, employer vesting tax deductions or excess tax benefits are credited. The full economic grant cost remains in DCF; lower treasury cash does not make the net-share award free.

Legacy cash is assumed at 365.2 for H2 FY2027, 730.4 in FY2028, 486.9333 in FY2029 and 243.4667 in FY2030. That is a historical-run-rate/attrition sensitivity, **not** an observed vesting schedule. The combined stress doubles it. Actual award quantities, taxes, stock values, vesting and settlement dates remain hard gates.

The **September 25 declaration** pays 0.06 on **October 29** to **October 9** holders. It is included in the treasury screen as a 53.92227678 stale-share-inventory proxy, including participating preferred. Exact October eligible shares/payable remain unknown. Only future undeclared distributions and repurchases are set to zero. The August-origin valuation bridge is not silently shifted to an ex-dividend October value.

A 300 forward cash outflow in March 2027 is a notional-scale adverse sensitivity, not a contractual maximum or forecast. The combined stress moves that payment to October 2026. The positive August 131 mark is never credited as spendable cash. Original forward confirmation, strike, cash formula and precise early-termination/maturity terms were not located in the reviewed filings; the quarterly note and risk factor give slightly different entry descriptions. These gaps prohibit a complete settlement claim.

Existing bonds pay their disclosed semiannual coupons and dated maturities. Cash-repayment cases retire the full 4,999.9 face. Alternative refinance cases explicitly replace every maturity with hypothetical five-year debt at 6.39%, paying 0.5% issuance fees, including subsequent rollovers. No capital-market availability is assured. Existing principal falls in FY2029 1,249.9; FY2030 500; FY2031 500; FY2032 750; FY2034 500; FY2036 500; FY2037 1,000.

The nominal 1,500 revolver ends in June 2030. Its contract moves a non-business-day fifth anniversary to the prior business day; the monthly screen uses June 28 as an assumption and permits no June-or-later draw. Remaining borrowing must be repaid in June, with no renewal. The 4.00× quarter-end covenant uses contractual debt and trailing contractual EBITDA, which cannot be inferred from the economic DCF. August compliance is not future access. Conditional cases alone permit nominal borrowing. Rate 6.39% is assumed; the reported 0.125% unused fee is held constant, accrued on a 360-day basis and paid quarterly. Opening July fee accrual is an explicit proxy, not a reported payable. Same-month draws fund their own interest; no interest tax shield is credited.

Within each period, baseline operating flows and investment are distributed uniformly. Monthly outflows are tested before positive monthly NOPAT. The severe timing case puts all annual nonresearch investment into the first month, doubles legacy withholding, advances the forward payment and adds 400 H2 capacity without displacing H2 other capital. This is not a daily treasury forecast. Bond business-day adjustments, actual fiscal-week alignment, future rating changes, all unknown balances and financing terms remain qualifications.

The corrected results do **not** support v1's blanket all-cases-funded statement. Base literal-cash compensation with cash debt repayment has a pre-financing gap of about 1,136.5; full refinancing removes that gap in base. Downside still has about 1,503.3 of gap even with full bond refinancing. All three illustrative equity-settlement/cash-repayment paths have no modeled gap under their assumptions, but that is not proof of actual adequacy. The severe timing cases have substantial gaps. After a first deficit, rows are unfunded cash-budget arithmetic; reported gaps exclude costs of financing that has not been identified. These are financing sensitivities, not demonstrated insolvency.
